input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 correctly leaves Customer Data and Customer IP with us, and Section 14.4 bars joint ownership, but Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer (§1.4) with only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables). The perpetual licence in §13.2 does not cure this: it covers Vendor Technology and paid-up software embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself. Redline flips the assignment to Customer while expressly preserving Vendor Technology under §14.3, with the paid-up perpetual licence offered as fallback.

ops.oldText: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: 14.2 Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon creation. Vendor retains Vendor Technology as provided in Section 14.3.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we commission, so we have flipped Section 14.2 to an assignment of Deliverables to Customer while leaving Vendor Technology with Vendor under Section 14.3. If assignment is not possible, we can accept Vendor ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence for us to use, modify, and sublicense Deliverables for our business.
proposal.summary: Reverse Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; Vendor retains Vendor Technology.
